newsitem.title: CHILE: Outokumpu Zaldivar copper pit buys plant.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu Zaldivar copper pit buys plant.

text.p: Chile's Minera Zaldivar copper mine, owned by Canadian mining company Placer Dome and Finland's Outokumpu Oy, said it will invest $28 million in 1997 in projects including a plant to treat fine mineral ores.
"These projects will allow us to meet our target production rate of 125,000 tonnes of copper per year at optimal efficiency," said deputy general manager Timothy Baker.

Mine officials said production will be 75,000 tonnes this year which is less than scheduled due to a high level of copper in fine mineral ore which cannot be processed using the mine's heap-leaching technology.
The pit, which lies in the northern Atacama Desert, will reach design capacity in the second half of 1997, said Baker.
